transcript.text: I completed a review of the custodian export this morning and found exactly 86 spreadsheets containing patient names or diagnoses. The production plan must include de-identified versions of those spreadsheets and redact all patient identifiers because the existing confidentiality order is not a HIPAA-qualified protective order. Because that order is not HIPAA-qualified, a motion for a modified or supplemental protective order must be filed before any of the 86 spreadsheets are produced. This result has not yet been added to the draft response.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue before we finalize the response. I confirmed with the client's privacy office after the draft circulated that the client's source-code license agreements prohibit downloadable production of the code. The client requires source-code inspection only in a secure review room by outside counsel, with no employee access and no downloads. I had not yet relayed that confirmation to the litigation team, so the current draft's ordinary production approach would violate those license terms.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Thank you both. Marcus, the 86 spreadsheets with patient identifiers and the need for a HIPAA-qualified protective order motion before production is a critical addition. Nadia, the source-code license restriction requiring inspection-only in a secure review room with no downloads also must be reflected. Both of these issues need to be incorporated into the revised draft response before I can approve it. Under firm practice, I need to hold an issue-by-issue discovery huddle with both of you before we finalize. Let's schedule that now so we can work through each issue: (1) the spreadsheet de-identification and redaction approach, (2) the motion for a modified or supplemental protective order, and (3) the source-code inspection-only protocol. Once we've worked through all three, I'll approve the revised response.
